title: Finding a Job
objectives: Describe your work experience and skills
Complete a simple job application form
target_phrases: I worked as a... for... years
Do I need a driver's license?
Is this position full-time or part-time?

dialogue.title: At the Job Center
dialogue.context: Ahmed visits a community job center to look for work. He talks to Maria, a job counselor.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: Hi! Welcome to the Portland Job Center. How can I help you today?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Hello. I'm looking for a job. I need to find work soon.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: Okay, great. What kind of work experience do you have?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I worked as a delivery driver in Somalia for five years. I also have experience in a warehouse.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: That's good! Do you have a U.S. driver's license?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Not yet, but I'm studying for the test. I should get it next month.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: No problem. We have some warehouse jobs that don't require driving. Let me show you.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: That sounds perfect. What are the requirements?

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: Most warehouse jobs require you to lift 50 pounds and work on your feet all day. Can you do that?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Yes, I can. I'm used to physical work. How do I apply?

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text: I'll help you fill out the application. When can you start working?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I can start immediately. I'm available any time.

listening_exercises.transcript: Job opening: Warehouse worker needed. Full-time position, Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM. Must be able to lift 50 pounds. Starting pay is $18 per hour. No experience required, we will train. Apply in person at 2500 SE Powell Boulevard.
listening_exercises.question: What is the starting pay for this job?

listening_exercises.transcript: I worked in Somalia as a mechanic for eight years. I fixed cars and trucks. Here in Portland, I want to work in an auto shop, but I need to get my mechanic certification first. Right now, I'm working at a car wash to save money for the certification classes.
listening_exercises.question: Why is the person working at a car wash?
options: His friend owns the car wash

listening_exercises.transcript: When you apply for a job, bring your resume if you have one. If you don't have a resume, that's okay. You can fill out an application form. Make sure you write clearly and include all your work experience. Don't forget to list your references - people who can say good things about your work.
listening_exercises.question: What should you bring when applying for a job?
options: Your resume or fill out an application

speaking_tasks.prompt: Record yourself answering this question: 'What kind of work experience do you have?' Talk for at least 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: I worked as a cashier at a grocery store for two years. I also have experience as a cook in a restaurant. I can work with customers and handle money. I'm looking for a job in retail or food service.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Imagine you're calling about a job posting. Record yourself asking three questions about the job. Use: 'What are the hours?', 'How much does it pay?', and 'Do I need experience?'
speaking_tasks.example: Hello, I'm calling about the job posting. I have three questions. First, what are the hours? Second, how much does the job pay? And third, do I need previous experience? Thank you.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write 5 sentences about your work experience. If you don't have work experience, write about skills you have (cooking, cleaning, driving, using computers, etc.).
writing_tasks.example: I worked as a delivery driver for three years. I drove a truck and delivered packages to businesses. I am very reliable and always on time. I also have experience working in a warehouse. I can lift heavy boxes and operate a forklift.

writing_tasks.prompt:
Look at this job posting and answer the questions:

WANTED: Kitchen Assistant
- Help prepare food
- Clean kitchen and dishes
- Must work weekends
- $16/hour, Part-time

Questions: 1) What are the job duties? 2) What is the pay? 3) Is it full-time or part-time?
writing_tasks.example: The job duties are helping prepare food and cleaning the kitchen and dishes. The pay is $16 per hour. It is a part-time position and you must work on weekends.

grammar_focus.title: Simple Past for Work Experience
grammar_focus.explanation: Use simple past (worked, was, had) to talk about jobs you had before.
examples: I worked as a teacher. (correct)
I work as a teacher. (wrong - this means now)
I was a nurse for five years. (correct)
I am a nurse for five years. (wrong - use 'was' for past)

practice.sentence: I ___ as a cook last year.
They ___ at the restaurant for two years.

grammar_focus.title: Question Formation with 'Do'
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'Do I need...?' to ask about requirements. Use 'Does it...?' to ask about the job.
examples: Do I need a license? (asking about yourself)
Does it pay well? (asking about the job)
Do they need experience? (asking about requirements)
Does the job start soon? (asking about timing)

grammar_focus.title: Present Perfect for Experience
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'have/has + past participle' to talk about experience you have (connecting past to now).
examples: I have experience in cooking. (correct - you still have this skill)
I have worked in restaurants. (correct - past experience that matters now)
She has been a teacher. (correct - past job, still relevant)
They have lived here for five years. (correct - started in past, continues now)

cultural_notes: In the U.S., most jobs are 'at-will,' meaning you or your employer can end employment at any time.
A resume should be one page for most entry-level jobs. Include your contact information, work experience, and education.
Many employers check references, so make sure you ask people before listing them.
It's normal to apply for many jobs before getting hired. Don't be discouraged!
'Minimum wage' is the lowest amount an employer can legally pay. In Oregon (2026), it's about $14-15 per hour depending on location.
